class ExactSparseMatrixBuilder(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ExactSparseMatrixBuilder, rows: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, columns: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, entries: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, force_dimensions: bool = True, has_custom_row_grouping: bool = False, row_groups: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0)¶

Builder of sparse matrix

add_next_value(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ExactSparseMatrixBuilder, row: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, column: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, value: stormpy.pycarl.gmp.Rational) → None¶

Sets the matrix entry at the given row and column to the given value. After all entries have been added, calling function build() is mandatory.

Note: this is a linear setter. That is, it must be called consecutively for each entry, row by row and column by column. As multiple entries per column are admitted, consecutive calls to this method are admitted to mention the same row-column-pair. If rows are skipped entirely, the corresponding rows are treated as empty. If these constraints are not met, an exception is thrown.

Parameters:

  • row (double) – The row in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • column (double) – The column in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • value (double) – The value that is to be set at the specified row and column

add_next_values(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ExactSparseMatrixBuilder, rows: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], cols: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], values: collections.abc.Sequence[stormpy.pycarl.gmp.Rational], row_group_indices: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex] = []) → None¶

Calls stormpy.storage.SparseMatrixBuilder.add_next_value() for each (row, col, value) triple. Accepts any sequence of scalars (e.g. plain Python lists).

Parameters:

  • rows (list[int]) – Row indices.

  • cols (list[int]) – Column indices.

  • values (list[float]) – Entry values.

  • row_group_indices (list[int]) – Starting row of each row group, in ascending order (optional).

build(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ExactSparseMatrixBuilder, overridden_row_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden_column_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden-row_group_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0) → storm::storage::SparseMatrix<__gmp_expr<__mpq_struct [1], __mpq_struct [1]> >¶

Finalize the sparse matrix

Start a new row group in the matrix

replace_columns(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ExactSparseMatrixBuilder, replacements: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], offset: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → None¶

Replaces all columns with id >= offset according to replacements. Every state with id offset+i is replaced by the id in replacements[i]. Afterwards the columns are sorted.

Parameters:

  • replacements (std::vector<double> const&) – replacements Mapping indicating the replacements from offset+i -> value of i

  • offset (int) – Offset to add to each id in vector index.

class ParametricSparseMatrixBuilder(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ParametricSparseMatrixBuilder, rows: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, columns: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, entries: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, force_dimensions: bool = True, has_custom_row_grouping: bool = False, row_groups: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0)¶

Builder of sparse matrix

add_next_value(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ParametricSparseMatrixBuilder, row: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, column: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, value: stormpy.pycarl.cln.FactorizedRationalFunction) → None¶

Sets the matrix entry at the given row and column to the given value. After all entries have been added, calling function build() is mandatory.

Note: this is a linear setter. That is, it must be called consecutively for each entry, row by row and column by column. As multiple entries per column are admitted, consecutive calls to this method are admitted to mention the same row-column-pair. If rows are skipped entirely, the corresponding rows are treated as empty. If these constraints are not met, an exception is thrown.

Parameters:

  • row (double) – The row in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • column (double) – The column in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • value (double) – The value that is to be set at the specified row and column

add_next_values(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ParametricSparseMatrixBuilder, rows: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], cols: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], values: collections.abc.Sequence[stormpy.pycarl.cln.FactorizedRationalFunction], row_group_indices: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex] = []) → None¶

Calls stormpy.storage.SparseMatrixBuilder.add_next_value() for each (row, col, value) triple. Accepts any sequence of scalars (e.g. plain Python lists).

Parameters:

  • rows (list[int]) – Row indices.

  • cols (list[int]) – Column indices.

  • values (list[float]) – Entry values.

  • row_group_indices (list[int]) – Starting row of each row group, in ascending order (optional).

build(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ParametricSparseMatrixBuilder, overridden_row_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden_column_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden-row_group_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0) → storm::storage::SparseMatrix<carl::RationalFunction<carl::FactorizedPolynomial<carl::MultivariatePolynomial<cln::cl_RA, carl::NotRelevant, carl::StdMultivariatePolynomialPolicies<0> > >, true> >¶

replace_columns(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ParametricSparseMatrixBuilder, replacements: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], offset: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → None¶

Replaces all columns with id >= offset according to replacements. Every state with id offset+i is replaced by the id in replacements[i]. Afterwards the columns are sorted.

Parameters:

  • replacements (std::vector<double> const&) – replacements Mapping indicating the replacements from offset+i -> value of i

  • offset (int) – Offset to add to each id in vector index.

class RationalIntervalSparseMatrixBuilder(self: stormpy.storage._storage.RationalIntervalSparseMatrixBuilder, rows: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, columns: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, entries: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, force_dimensions: bool = True, has_custom_row_grouping: bool = False, row_groups: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0)¶

Builder of sparse matrix

add_next_value(self: stormpy.storage._storage.RationalIntervalSparseMatrixBuilder, row: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, column: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, value: stormpy.pycarl.gmp.Interval) → None¶

Sets the matrix entry at the given row and column to the given value. After all entries have been added, calling function build() is mandatory.

Note: this is a linear setter. That is, it must be called consecutively for each entry, row by row and column by column. As multiple entries per column are admitted, consecutive calls to this method are admitted to mention the same row-column-pair. If rows are skipped entirely, the corresponding rows are treated as empty. If these constraints are not met, an exception is thrown.

Parameters:

  • row (double) – The row in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • column (double) – The column in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • value (double) – The value that is to be set at the specified row and column

add_next_values(self: stormpy.storage._storage.RationalIntervalSparseMatrixBuilder, rows: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], cols: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], values: collections.abc.Sequence[stormpy.pycarl.gmp.Interval], row_group_indices: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex] = []) → None¶

Calls stormpy.storage.SparseMatrixBuilder.add_next_value() for each (row, col, value) triple. Accepts any sequence of scalars (e.g. plain Python lists).

Parameters:

  • rows (list[int]) – Row indices.

  • cols (list[int]) – Column indices.

  • values (list[float]) – Entry values.

  • row_group_indices (list[int]) – Starting row of each row group, in ascending order (optional).

build(self: stormpy.storage._storage.RationalIntervalSparseMatrixBuilder, overridden_row_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden_column_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden-row_group_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0) → storm::storage::SparseMatrix<carl::Interval<__gmp_expr<__mpq_struct [1], __mpq_struct [1]> > >¶

Finalize the sparse matrix

Get the current row group count

replace_columns(self: stormpy.storage._storage.RationalIntervalSparseMatrixBuilder, replacements: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], offset: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → None¶

Replaces all columns with id >= offset according to replacements. Every state with id offset+i is replaced by the id in replacements[i]. Afterwards the columns are sorted.

Parameters:

  • replacements (std::vector<double> const&) – replacements Mapping indicating the replacements from offset+i -> value of i

  • offset (int) – Offset to add to each id in vector index.

class SparseMatrixBuilder(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder, rows: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, columns: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, entries: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0, force_dimensions: bool = True, has_custom_row_grouping: bool = False, row_groups: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex = 0)¶

Builder of sparse matrix

add_next_value(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder, row: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, column: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, value: SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex) → None¶

Sets the matrix entry at the given row and column to the given value. After all entries have been added, calling function build() is mandatory.

Note: this is a linear setter. That is, it must be called consecutively for each entry, row by row and column by column. As multiple entries per column are admitted, consecutive calls to this method are admitted to mention the same row-column-pair. If rows are skipped entirely, the corresponding rows are treated as empty. If these constraints are not met, an exception is thrown.

Parameters:

  • row (double) – The row in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • column (double) – The column in which the matrix entry is to be set

  • value (double) – The value that is to be set at the specified row and column

add_next_values(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder, rows: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], cols: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], values: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsFloat | SupportsIndex], row_group_indices: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex] = []) → None¶

Calls stormpy.storage.SparseMatrixBuilder.add_next_value() for each (row, col, value) triple. Accepts any sequence of scalars (e.g. plain Python lists).

Parameters:

  • rows (list[int]) – Row indices.

  • cols (list[int]) – Column indices.

  • values (list[float]) – Entry values.

  • row_group_indices (list[int]) – Starting row of each row group, in ascending order (optional).

build(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder, overridden_row_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden_column_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0, overridden-row_group_count: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex = 0) → storm::storage::SparseMatrix<double>¶

Finalize the sparse matrix

get_last_column(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder) → int¶

the most recently used column

get_last_row(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder) → int¶

Get the most recently used row

new_row_group(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder, starting_row: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → None¶

Start a new row group in the matrix

replace_columns(self: stormpy.storage._storage.SparseMatrixBuilder, replacements: collections.abc.Sequence[SupportsInt | SupportsIndex], offset: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex) → None¶

Replaces all columns with id >= offset according to replacements. Every state with id offset+i is replaced by the id in replacements[i]. Afterwards the columns are sorted.

Parameters:

  • replacements (std::vector<double> const&) – replacements Mapping indicating the replacements from offset+i -> value of i

  • offset (int) – Offset to add to each id in vector index.

class StateValuationsBuilder(*args, **kwargs)¶

Deprecated shim for the old state-valuations builder API.

Buffers the variables and per-state values passed via add_variable/add_state, and only constructs the new ValuationDescriptionBuilder/Valuations objects once build() is called (integer bounds are derived automatically from the buffered values, since the new API requires them upfront but the old one did not).

Deprecated since version 1.13.2: Use ValuationDescriptionBuilder and Valuations instead.

add_state(state, boolean_values=None, integer_values=None, rational_values=None)¶

Adds a new state, no more variables should be added afterwards. :param state: State. :param boolean_values: Values for the boolean variables, in the order they were added. :param integer_values: Values for the integer variables, in the order they were added. :param rational_values: Values for the rational variables, in the order they were added.

add_variable(variable)¶

Adds a new variable. :param variable: Variable.

class ValuationTransformer(self: stormpy.storage._storage.ValuationTransformer, old_valuations: stormpy.storage._storage.Valuations)¶

Transforms the given valuations to a new valuations over a new variable set. The values of the new variables are determined by evaluating the provided expressions w.r.t. the old variable valuation. The freshly introduced variables may either replace or extend the existing variable set.

get_boolean_values_states_as_bitvector(self: stormpy.storage._storage.Valuations, variable: storm::expressions::Variable) → stormpy.storage._storage.BitVector¶

Get the Boolean variable value for all entities as a BitVector, with no per-entity list conversion. More efficient than get_values_states for large models, but note that iterating the result yields the indices of the entities where the value is true, not a per-entity true/false sequence.

get_double_value(self: stormpy.storage._storage.Valuations, entity: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, variable: storm::expressions::Variable) → float¶

Get the value of a rational variable that was declared with the double (64-bit IEEE754) storage encoding via add_double_variable, as a Python float. get_value/get_rational_value assume the exact encoding and cannot read a double-encoded variable.

get_double_values_states(self: stormpy.storage._storage.Valuations, variable: storm::expressions::Variable) → list[float]¶

Get the value for all entities of a rational variable declared via add_double_variable.

get_integer_bigint_value(self: stormpy.storage._storage.Valuations, entity: SupportsInt | SupportsIndex, variable: storm::expressions::Variable) → stormpy.pycarl.gmp.Integer¶

Get the value of an integer variable as an arbitrary-precision integer. Only needed for integer variables declared with arbitrary-precision bounds whose value does not fit in an int64; get_value already handles the common case.
